/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 142

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture142

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 142](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/):

For a simple connected graph $G$,
$\mathrm{tree}(G) \ge (2/3) \cdot \mathrm{girth}(G) + \mathrm{ecc}(B)$
where $\mathrm{tree}(G)$ is the largest induced tree size, $\mathrm{girth}(G)$
is the length of the shortest cycle ($0$ if acyclic), $B$ is the set of
boundary vertices (those of maximum eccentricity), and $\mathrm{ecc}(B)$ is
the eccentricity of the set $B$.

**Proof sketch.** The proof first strengthens the real-valued target to the
integral bound
$$
\mathrm{ecc}(B) + \mathrm{girth}(G)
  - \lfloor \mathrm{girth}(G) / 3 \rfloor \leq \mathrm{tree}(G).
$$
For a cyclic graph, start with a shortest cycle $K$. It is chordless, so
removing one vertex leaves an induced path on $\mathrm{girth}(G)-1$ vertices.
Shortest paths from selected vertices to $K$ are called *descents*. Pairwise
noninteracting descents attach to the retained cycle path as disjoint branches.
If two descents interact, the proof cuts at the first interaction encountered
from the outer endpoint toward the cycle and splices the paths there.
Minimality of that interaction makes the retained prefix disjoint and
nonadjacent to the first descent; geodesicity excludes chords, while girth at
least five rules out extra cross-edges and cycle attachments.

Choose a vertex realizing $\mathrm{ecc}(B)$ and two endpoints of a diametral
geodesic. Either two of their descents interact, directly giving a sufficiently
long spliced tree, or all three are separate, in which case a three-point
distance inequality forces their total length to be large enough. This proves
the integral bound in the main range. Girths three and four, small
$\mathrm{ecc}(B)$, and the two remaining congruence cases are handled by
separate geodesic/cycle certificates with one or two descents; the acyclic case
follows from a diametral path. Finally,
$$
\mathrm{girth}(G)-\lfloor\mathrm{girth}(G)/3\rfloor
  = \lceil 2\,\mathrm{girth}(G)/3\rceil
  \geq 2\,\mathrm{girth}(G)/3,
$$
which gives the stated real-valued inequality.

The argument was developed with assistance from ChatGPT Pro. The linked Lean 4
formalization was produced with assistance from OpenAI Codex and checked by
Lean.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/AlperTheKing/formal-conjectures/blob/46bf39015f5c3c3ba3bfcf9f752b4b1e49b584ac/FormalConjecturesForMathlib/WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture142Proof.lean#L3927-L3932"]
theorem conjecture142 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    let B : Set α := (maxEccentricityVertices G : Set α)
    (2 : ℝ) / 3 * (G.girth : ℝ) + (eccSet G B : ℝ) ≤ (largestInducedTreeSize G : ℝ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `largestInducedTreeSize` is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ largestInducedTreeSize G := Nat.zero_le _

/-- `eccSet G` returns a natural number (nonneg). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    0 ≤ eccSet G (maxEccentricityVertices G) :=
  Nat.zero_le _

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture142

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement uses `eccSet G B`, the maximum of the distance to B over ALL vertices of G, vertices of B included. WOWII definition 52 defines ecc(S) as "the maximum of distances from vertices of V-S to the set S", i.e. it leaves out the vertices of S. When V∖B is empty (self-centred graphs, e.g. cycles or complete graphs), the source's maximum is over the empty set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every vertex v ∈ B has distance 0 to B, because dist v v = 0. So adding these vertices to the maximum cannot change it when V∖B is nonempty. When V∖B is empty, both quantities are 0 (`eccSet` because every term is 0; the repository's `ecc`, which is literally definition 52, returns 0 by its own convention). I proved `eccSet G S = ecc G S` for every graph and every S in a scratch file (lemmas `distToSet_eq_zero_of_mem'`, `eccSet_eq_sup'`, `ecc_eq_sup'`, `eccSet_eq_ecc'`); `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. In the empty case the claim becomes (2/3)·girth ≤ tree(G), which holds anyway since tree(G) ≥ girth − 1 (repo lemma `girth_sub_one_le_largestInducedTreeSize`). So no reading of the empty maximum changes the truth of the statement.

reformulations.difference: Mathlib's `G.girth` is 0 for acyclic graphs. WOWII definition 43 only says "the number of vertices of a smallest cycle of the graph" and gives no value for acyclic graphs. Separately, `[Nontrivial α]` excludes the one-vertex graph, which the source's "simple connected graph" allows.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If G has a cycle, Mathlib's girth is the length of a shortest cycle, which equals the number of its vertices, so the two statements coincide. If G is a tree, the Lean inequality reads ecc(B) ≤ tree(G) = n. This always holds, since ecc(B) ≤ diam(G) ≤ n − 1. So the Lean statement is the source's claim on graphs with a cycle, plus instances that are true anyway. A convention girth(tree) = ∞ is ruled out: Graffiti.pc's database contains trees (e.g. K2), which would refute the conjecture at once. WOWII also marks as proved conjectures 48 (f(G) ≥ girth(G) + f₁(G) − 1) and 197, which would fail for trees under that convention. For K1 the source's claim reads 0 + 0 ≤ 1, so the `Nontrivial` restriction is harmless. I proved in Lean that `maxEccentricityVertices G` is exactly the set of vertices of maximum eccentricity (definition 55), and that acyclic ⇒ girth = 0. The tree case itself I argued by hand; the linked formal proof covers the whole statement.

review.notes:
What the source poses. WOWII Conjecture 142 is "If G is a simple connected graph, then tree(G) ≥ (2/3)*girth + ecc(B)". Its definitions: tree(G) = order of a largest induced tree (def 48); girth = number of vertices of a smallest cycle (def 43); ecc(S) = maximum distance from a vertex of V−S to S (def 52); B = the periphery, i.e. the vertices of maximum eccentricity, "previously called here set of boundary vertices" (def 55). The docstring's "boundary vertices (those of maximum eccentricity)" therefore uses WOWII's old name correctly; it is not the Chartrand et al. notion of boundary vertex. The live URLs (cms.dt.uh.edu and cms.uhd.edu) time out over HTTPS; I read the Wayback snapshots listed.

Status. The source's latest snapshot (2026-07-23) still marks 142 "O" ("open (as far as I know)"). The file's `research solved` rests on the linked 2026 Lean proof, which matches the repository convention (solved = formally proved here or elsewhere). I checked that proof: I fetched the pinned file and fixed it only for API changes in the current Mathlib/checkout. Specifically, `Walk.rotate` and `mem_support_rotate_iff`/`rotate_edges` now take the vertex explicitly; `G.loopless` became `G.loopless.irrefl`; one `0 < f` to `1 ≤ f` step needed `Nat.succ_le_of_lt`; and I renamed two lemmas that were later upstreamed into LargestInducedTree.lean. With these fixes it compiles against this checkout with 0 errors. `#print axioms` on the linked theorem gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and `example : type_of% @WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture142.conjecture142 := @FormalProofs.WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture142.conjecture142` typechecks, so it proves exactly the repository statement. The file is therefore ahead of the source, not stale, and I report no status issue.

Minor metadata, not mathematics: the `formal_proof` kind is `formal_conjectures` although the proof lives only in a personal fork; `lean4` might fit CONTRIBUTING's wording better, but sibling WOWII files use the same pattern. Also, the unmodified pinned file no longer compiles against the current Mathlib; that is expected for a link pinned to a commit.

The two `test` examples are trivial `Nat.zero_le` facts and are correct.
